questions.title: @Transactional in practice
questions.prompt: How does @Transactional work in Spring, and what are the common pitfalls?
expectedConcepts: Default rollback only on unchecked exceptions
Annotations on non-public methods are ignored by proxy-based AOP
Transaction boundaries belong in the service layer
questions.answerOutline: Explain the proxy model, then the pitfalls: self-invocation, checked exceptions, catching exceptions inside the method, long transactions holding connections, and calling remote services inside a transaction.
followUps: How do you test transactional behaviour?
questions.rubricNotes: 5: explains the proxy mechanism and at least three pitfalls with fixes.

questions.title: Life of a request
questions.prompt: Walk me through what happens when an HTTP request hits a Spring Boot REST endpoint.
expectedConcepts: Servlet filter chain, including Spring Security
questions.answerOutline: Tomcat accepts the connection, runs the filters (security), then DispatcherServlet finds the handler, binds and validates the body, invokes the controller, and serialises the result. Exceptions go to the advice.
followUps: Where would you add request logging with a correlation ID?
How do virtual threads change this?
questions.rubricNotes: Order of components matters more than naming every class.

questions.title: Diagnosing slow JPA endpoints
questions.prompt: An endpoint listing orders with customer names got slow as data grew. How do you investigate and fix it?
expectedConcepts: JOIN FETCH / entity graphs / DTO projections
questions.answerOutline: Reproduce, count queries, identify N+1, fix it with fetch joins or projections, add pagination, and verify indexes and plans.
commonMistakes: JOIN FETCH with pagination on collections (in-memory pagination warning)
followUps: Why is EAGER fetching a poor global fix?
How would you prevent regressions? (query count assertions)
